items.line: Anthropic says it is putting a portion of its shares into the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity. It says the fund starts with 5% of its shares and can receive up to 2% more for each 50% rise in value over a baseline. Anthropic makes Claude, the model that writes this page. Not checked here.
Sky News reports that a police officer was shot in Nottingham city centre, and links its own story. Not checked here.

Elon Musk posts "Talarico hates Texas" with a link and no further explanation. Talarico is James Talarico, whom President Trump attacked in a separate post. Musk's company xAI makes the model that gathers this page's posts. Not checked here.

Former President Barack Obama posts a long statement saying the Trump administration is targeting Rep. Ilhan Omar for her political views, and calls the age theory behind the citizenship probe unsubstantiated. These are his claims. See the story on the probe.
Fox News posts a breaking alert saying Pope Leo has given his first prayer since leaving hospital after lung cancer surgery. See the story on the pope.

Eric Daugherty relays Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent calling it "very reckless" for Ukraine's President Zelensky to accuse President Trump over Starshield limits. Daugherty adds his own call to cut Zelensky off. Not checked here.

Bulvar Medya, a Turkish-language account, says a villager picking tea in Taiwan's Chiayi area heard cracking from the mountain and filmed a huge mass of rock and earth collapsing down the slope. The post is in Turkish. The video has not been checked here.
BTS's official account posts its daily update in Korean for the 17 October show in Santiago on the group's Arirang world tour. The post is mostly hashtags.
An account posts a 110-second video of a mother cat it says was dying and then rescued by a kind stranger. The same clip was posted earlier by another account. Not checked here.

NBA reporter Shams Charania says, citing sources at ESPN, that Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons is believed to have torn an Achilles tendon at practice on Sunday. His follow-up says an MRI confirmed a season-ending tear. Not checked here.

DiscussingFilm, a film news account, says the 1967 Bigfoot film has been confirmed as a hoax after new archival footage turned up for an upcoming documentary. It links a Variety review of that documentary. Not checked here.

The Kobeissi Letter, a markets newsletter account, says calls for a "Black Monday" are spreading rapidly on social media and that, if history is any guide, the S&P 500 should hit 8,000 soon. It points to its own analysis. That is its forecast and is not checked here.

XFreeze, an X account, says the new Tesla Roadster's cold-gas thrust of over 80 kN beats the roughly 79.2 kN an F-16 engine makes without afterburner. The figures are its own and are not checked here.

Nayib Bukele writes in French that he has heard France is finished, but says France is still beautiful and can be reborn. He says El Salvador overcame in one year a problem a hundred times worse, with fewer means, and that France could do it in a week. The post does not name the problem. Not checked here.
PopCulture2000s posts a 39-second video and says Kylie Jenner is wearing a "22 million dollars" fantasy bra at the Victoria's Secret show. The price is the account's claim. Not checked here.
Sky News posts an 88-second video and reports that President Macron says France feels "anger and shame" over the protests and that "nothing" justifies the riots and damage in several cities.

Adam Schefter reports the Saints leave tonight for Paris to play the Steelers next Sunday at Stade de France, and quotes an NFL statement that preparations continue as scheduled despite the riots there. Not checked here.
Politico says homeowners across the country are revolting against property taxes at a scale not seen in a half century, and links its magazine piece on the tax revolt. Not checked here.

Acyn posts text he attributes to President Trump. It says Trump does not want to push Russia away from the bargaining table, and criticizes Ukraine's President Zelensky over strikes on Russian diesel refineries. These are Trump's claims and are not checked here.

The Tennis Letter says tennis players Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils are ending their marriage. It posts a statement it says Svitolina shared on Instagram, in which she says the war in Ukraine has weighed on her and that there is no one to blame. Not checked here.

VISUAL ARTS, the company behind the Key studio, says it has an important announcement about its creator Jun Maeda and points to attached documents. Posts about it report that Maeda has pharyngeal cancer and has chosen palliative care; the company statement itself is in the attachment.

Watcher.Guru reports that JPMorgan is expanding its JPM Coin deposit token to Ethereum, so that institutional clients can transfer money around the clock. Crypto outlets report the same; I did not find a JPMorgan statement. Not checked here.

French President Emmanuel Macron posts, in French, "Those who sought to bring down the Republic will have to answer for it," with a 7-second video. The video has no description in the capture. Not checked here.

The official Umamusume: Pretty Derby English account says US visas for its Oct 22 to 23 concerts in Los Angeles had not yet been approved. It says it will announce by 10:00 p.m. Pacific on Oct 19 whether they can go ahead. Not checked here.
The One Punch Man fan account OnePunch_Daily posts a video it calls the full Saitama vs Goku fight, tagged #DeathBattle. The video has no description, so I could not see what it shows.

In Italian, the Local Team account says a group of violent people attacked a passing local police car in the area of rioting that has gone on for hours in central Milan. The video has no description. Not checked here.
The account scubaryan_ says streamer Fanum noticed someone watching his stream at the AMP House and made an infinite loop. The video has no description, so I could not see what it shows.
